vulnerabilities.name: DOM XSS via innerHTML/outerHTML Assignment
vulnerabilities.description: An attacker-influenced value (URL fragment, query string, postMessage data, referrer) flows into .innerHTML, .outerHTML, or insertAdjacentHTML without sanitization, letting injected markup execute as script.
vulnerabilities.notes: Flag when a source pattern feeds, directly or via a short variable chain, into a sink pattern within the same script/function without an intervening encode/sanitize call (e.g. textContent, DOMPurify.sanitize, encodeURIComponent).

vulnerabilities.name: DOM XSS via eval / Function Constructor / Timer String Argument
vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted data is passed as a string into eval(), new Function(), setTimeout(string), or setInterval(string), causing it to be parsed and executed as JavaScript.
vulnerabilities.notes: A CSP without unsafe-eval blocks this sink class at runtime even if the pattern exists in source; check CSP first before flagging as exploitable.

vulnerabilities.name: DOM XSS via javascript: URI in Location/Href Sink
vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted input is concatenated into location, location.href, location.assign(), location.replace(), window.open(), or an anchor's href without validating the scheme, allowing a javascript: URI to execute on click or immediately.
vulnerabilities.notes: Confirmed when no allow-list scheme check (e.g. startsWith('http')) precedes assignment to the sink.

vulnerabilities.name: DOM XSS via jQuery html()/append()/before()/after()
vulnerabilities.description: jQuery DOM-manipulation methods that parse their argument as HTML are called with attacker-influenced data, mirroring the native innerHTML sink risk.
vulnerabilities.notes: jQuery's .text() is the safe counterpart; flag only the HTML-parsing variants listed in sinks.

vulnerabilities.name: DOM XSS via postMessage Listener Without Origin Validation
vulnerabilities.description: A message event listener consumes event.data and writes it into a dangerous sink without first checking event.origin against an allow-list, letting any embedding/framing page or popup inject content.
vulnerabilities.notes: Flag when the listener body uses event.data/e.data without a preceding `if (event.origin !== ...)` or `=== ` allow-list check.

vulnerabilities.name: Angular bypassSecurityTrust* Misuse
vulnerabilities.description: Angular's DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml/Script/Style/Url/ResourceUrl is called with attacker-influenced data, deliberately opting the value out of Angular's built-in auto-sanitization.

vulnerabilities.name: React dangerouslySetInnerHTML with Unsanitized Data
vulnerabilities.description: A React component passes attacker-influenced data into the dangerouslySetInnerHTML prop without first passing it through a sanitizer such as DOMPurify.
vulnerabilities.notes: Not a finding if the __html value is wrapped in DOMPurify.sanitize(...) or an equivalent allow-listing sanitizer.

vulnerabilities.name: Vue v-html Directive with Unsanitized Binding
vulnerabilities.description: A Vue template binds v-html to a value derived from route params, query strings, or API responses without sanitization, rendering it as raw HTML.

vulnerabilities.name: DOM XSS via iframe srcdoc Built From Untrusted Input
vulnerabilities.description: An iframe's srcdoc attribute is constructed by string concatenation/template literal using attacker-influenced data, executing injected markup inside the iframe's document.

vulnerabilities.name: DOM XSS via localStorage/sessionStorage Read Into Sink (Stored-DOM Hybrid)
vulnerabilities.description: A value previously written to localStorage/sessionStorage (potentially by an attacker via a separate same-origin weakness, or shared across subdomains) is read back and passed into a dangerous sink without sanitization.

vulnerabilities.name: Reflected XSS: Unescaped Parameter Echoed in HTML Body
vulnerabilities.description: A query-string or form parameter is written back into the server-rendered HTML response without context-appropriate encoding, so angle brackets and quotes in the input pass through unescaped.

reflection_indicators.<[^>]*>: raw angle-bracket markup echoing a request parameter's literal value, unescaped, inside the HTML body or an attribute

vulnerabilities.notes: Confirmed by injecting a unique marker containing <, >, " and ' into each parameter and checking whether all four characters survive unescaped at the reflection point.

vulnerabilities.name: Stored XSS: User-Supplied Content Rendered Without Sanitization
vulnerabilities.description: Content submitted by one user (comment, profile field, support ticket, filename) is persisted and later rendered to other users' browsers without server-side sanitization or output encoding, so injected markup executes for every viewer.

reflection_indicators.<[^>]*>: raw angle-bracket markup from a previously stored field appearing unescaped on a page viewed by a different session/user than the one who submitted it

vulnerabilities.notes: Distinguish from reflected XSS by confirming the payload persists across requests/sessions and renders for a second, independent viewer.

vulnerabilities.name: Missing or Weak Content-Security-Policy Allowing Inline Script
vulnerabilities.description: The response has no Content-Security-Policy header, or one that still permits 'unsafe-inline'/'unsafe-eval' or a wildcard script-src, removing the browser-side defense-in-depth layer that would otherwise block most XSS payloads from executing even if an injection point exists.
vulnerabilities.notes: This is a mitigation-gap finding, not an injection point itself; pair it with a confirmed sink/source or reflection finding above to assess real exploitability.

vulnerabilities.name: Missing X-Content-Type-Options Enabling MIME Sniffing to HTML
vulnerabilities.description: A response that returns user-influenced content with a non-HTML or missing Content-Type can be MIME-sniffed by the browser as text/html when X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is absent, turning an otherwise inert download/response into an executable XSS vector.
